notes:
Stage: evaluation — mid-market analytics SaaS building a contextual search + support assistant. Customer currently on another major LLM API provider; wants migration path to Redwood Hosted then Dedicated once parity proven.

POC summary: migrated 2 endpoints (support-chat, doc-summarize) behind Redwood openai-compat shim. Early wins: 15% lower p95 token latency on hosted-ml-large variant; built-in KV prefix caching reduced repeated-doc cost 30%. Issues: prompt parity failures in abstractive summarization (shorter outputs, misses bullet points), tokenizer differences affecting entity boundaries in rerank tests.

Quoted from CTO (Aaron Delgado): "We can tolerate small output variance but hallucination/regression risk needs threshold — <1% bad outputs in high-risk flows." Head of ML (Priya Shah) asked for quantitative parity (ROUGE/ROUGE-L/EM) and a per-prompt diff tool.

Workstreams: prompt parity shim + tokenization adapter, extended regression run (2 weeks) with golden prompts, canary on Dedicated with autoscale/burst profiling, fallback policy to incumbent for risky routes. SE suggested quantization profiles for Dedicated to reduce cost with minimal regressions.

Links: pricing deck (drive), security FAQ (drive), call recordings (fireflies ids). Next commercial asks: clear TCO comparison, SLA (p95 targets), and a migration checklist (compat hooks, rate limits, retries).
additional_context:
Latency target: p95 <=200ms for chat non-streaming in NA region (for small context). Throughput target: 60-100 qps across endpoints during peak. Cost sensitivity: mid — willing to commit for predictable pricing if regressions are resolved. Evaluating Redwood's Optimize recommendations for batching + KV caching.

Migration specifics: currently heavy use of OpenAI-style prompt templates with few-shot examples. Key technical blocker is prompt parity: need same tokenization and stop-sequence behavior; Redwood provided a compat layer but found edge-case outputs. SE recommended prompt reshaping and a golden-suite automated comparator.

Legal/compliance: require data residency guidance for EU customers, KMS support for encryption-at-rest, and audit log retention 7 years for certain customers.
